title: The 8 Levels of Remote Work
house: A bustling metropolitan city made of glass skyscrapers, coffee shops, and fiber-optic cables, inhabited by living fruit and vegetable people.
links: A quiet blueberry barista in Level 2 mentions a stressed broccoli always ordering double espresso.
A coconut manager in Level 5 complains about a glitchy microphone from the broccoli in Level 8.

levels.open_loop: Why did the system lock my Slack account right during the quarterly review?

gegenspieler.tat: Muted her microphone during the presentation and laughed at her broken headset.

levels.name: Sam, 22, Intern
levels.story: The 8 levels of remote work. Level 1. Level 1: 1,200 dollars a month and my Wi-Fi drops every five minutes. I stared at my cracked laptop screen in the dark closet. You are lagging so hard, everyone is laughing at your camera feed! I gripped my $4 thrifted headphones. Then the screen froze completely. You look like a joke on corporate calls. My digital badge pulsed red. Suddenly, my direct deposit notification popped up. Wait, why does it say zero? You'll see that in Level 2.

levels.name: Mia, 26, Copywriter
levels.story: The 8 levels of remote work. Level 2. Level 2: 2,400 dollars a month and my client demands revisions at midnight. I typed furiously while boiling instant ramen on a hot plate. Your copy lacks soul, just like your tiny apartment. I stared at my second-hand monitor held up by old textbooks. Then, my phone buzzed with an incoming wire transfer. Who authorized this sudden bonus? You'll see that in Level 3.

levels.name: Leo, 31, Developer
levels.story: The 8 levels of remote work. Level 3. Level 3: 4,100 dollars a month and I am debugging production code at 3 AM. I rubbed my stinging eyes in front of three monitors displaying endless terminal text. Fix that memory leak before the Tokyo team logs on, or else. I slammed my fist on the wooden desk, spilling my cold coffee. Why is everyone treating me like an intern? Who just deleted my root access? You'll see that in Level 4.

levels.name: Chloe, 29, Product Manager
levels.story: The 8 levels of remote work. Level 4. Level 4: 6,200 dollars a month and I am mediating a screaming match on Zoom. Six different fruit avatars were shouting over each other about feature roadmaps. You are losing control of this team, Chloe, management is noticing. I pressed mute and took a deep breath. My hands shook on my wireless mouse. I had worked eighty hours this week. Who forwarded my private performance review to the whole company? You'll see that in Level 5.

levels.name: Victoria, 38, VP of Operations
levels.story: The 8 levels of remote work. Level 6. Level 6: 12,500 dollars a month and I am firing three department heads over a Zoom webinar. I looked into the camera lens with absolute coldness. You can cut all the staff you want, Victoria, but your division is still bankrupt. I gripped the edges of my mahogany desk so hard my knuckles turned white. My digital badge shone with an blinding platinum light. Who just bought out my entire division behind my back? You'll see that in Level 7.

levels.story: The 8 levels of remote work. Level 7. Level 7: 22,000 dollars a month and I am orchestrating a hostile corporate takeover from my yacht. Power isn't ethical, it's arithmetic. Who emptied my offshore account in three seconds? You'll see that in Level 8.
